name: Oxide-stabilized silicon surfaces
summary: Measurements showing that a thermally grown oxide layer gives silicon surfaces stable electrical behaviour, which made reliable silicon transistors and MOS devices possible.
description: Atalla, Tannenbaum and Scheibner measured thermally oxidized silicon interfaces and device behavior, finding stable surface potentials with characteristic interface states.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.

impact.note: A finding used by the semiconductor profession that made stable silicon devices possible; MOS and planar device work grew from it.

why: Transistor characteristics drifted because silicon surfaces were electrically unstable; Bardeen's surface-state ideas pointed to the surface as the cause.
